digest.component_or_area: plan-review close gate and completion verification
propositions: Adding the [operator-attested] tag to an acceptance criterion in the description after plan certification edits the material, invalidating the signed plan-review attestation as stale-material before completion verification can run.

Completion-verifier remediation guidance instructs users to add the [operator-attested] tag and record evidence in a comment, then re-verify, but this sequence triggers a material-staleness rejection at the plan-review close gate.
For deletion or renaming tickets where the old plan describes code the change removes, a fresh plan review cannot pass on the same text because the premises are factually obsolete post-delivery.
The design intends evidence-kind classification to occur before plan certification, with the tag present in the initial plan, not added afterward as a material edit.
Comments are non-material and do not invalidate plan-review attestations, but adding the marker token to the description text does, creating a guidance conflict between the two gates.

No automatic code repair is appropriate because the stale-material behavior is intended anti-tamper protection; a design decision is required to resolve whether evidence-kind must be declared early, represented outside mutable text, or permitted as a late post-review transformation.
